correctness.rationale: For the exact symmetric local squeezed-bath Lindbladian, the normal occupation is N times the identity and the anomalous second-moment matrix has an explicitly solved, unique linear steady state. The real quadrature covariance and all needed block determinants are derived in RESULT.md. The two-mode Gaussian partial-transpose formula yields the exact smallest symplectic eigenvalue for every relative bath phase. Strict positivity of the second derivative establishes the unique phase optimum, threshold and equality cases; the entanglement window follows by sign-preserving squaring to a quadratic and the high-squeezing phase asymptotic follows by arccosine expansion. Exact finite symbolic checks in check_symbolic.py and 1500 separately computed numerical Lyapunov/eigenspectrum comparisons in verify.py passed; these computations are cross-checks, not the infinite-parameter proof. The stated model assumptions and physical boundaries are explicit.

originality.rationale: Ayoub et al. arXiv:2605.03978v1, equations (2), (5)-(6) and (12)-(17), already provide the model and the aligned-phase smallest partial-transpose eigenvalue, while figures 1-2 give qualitative phase maps and fixed-phase squeezing domes. Our aligned limit reduces exactly to their formula, but their specialized expression is not itself a general arbitrary-phase covariance law and does not supply optimization over relative phase, a strictly positive infinite-squeezing optimum, or the exact exponentially small entangled phase window. Bittner arXiv:2511.19662v1 studies the overlapping two-bath Gaussian model in entropy and exceptional-point terms, without a corresponding Gaussian-PPT optimization theorem. Both primary documents were materially inspected. Targeted scientific record and published-source searches located no dominating all-phase equivalent. This is a positive claim-vs-prior implication comparison, not novelty by failed search; residual unindexed or algebraically implicit equivalents are explicitly acknowledged.

value.rationale: The motivating quantum reservoir problem identifies the phase reference as experimentally controllable and an aligned finite-squeezing entanglement dome. The new theorem exposes the precise advantage and cost of adjusting two local bath phases: the optimal logarithmic negativity becomes independent of squeezing strength above an exact threshold, provided the bath occupancy is below an exact cutoff, yet the successful phase window collapses exponentially as squeezing increases. This reconciles the apparent high-squeezing loss under fixed phase with phase control and gives an exact, physically interpretable precision-versus-resource frontier rather than a marginal numeric improvement or arbitrary slice.
